A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CompassNav and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–G. Content can be matched reliably across the reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original navigation experiments, training and reward ablations, memory experiments, and qualitative physical-robot results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds NavNuances, ProcTHOR, and training-hyperparameter experiments.

M1.justification: The SFT-then-GRPO procedure, gap-aware reward, action proposal and backtracking mechanisms, masked decoding, and stopping agent are unchanged. Expanded descriptions and experimental training variants do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: V2 adds NavNuances tasks testing direction changes, numerical comprehension, landmark and region recognition, and vertical movement. It also adds evaluation in unseen synthetic ProcTHOR environments, extending coverage beyond the retained HM3D/MP3D navigation tasks and physical-robot demonstrations.

E2.justification: New comparisons include NavGPT-3.5, NavGPT-4, and NavGPT-4V in Table 3, plus EmbCLIP and the ProcTHOR agent in Table 7. Conversely, the SoftMax reward comparator in v1 Table 4b is removed from v2 Table 5b. The earlier main benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments specify over 8,000 unseen episodes using Habitat-compatible ProcTHOR, adaptive versus fixed KL regularization, and GRPO group sizes of 3, 5, and 7. The retained experiments preserve their splits, SR/SPL metrics, training budgets, and stopping criteria; the default training configuration remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds synthetic-domain transfer testing and sensitivity analyses investigating KL strategy and GRPO group size in Appendix A.1. These substantially broaden robustness evidence. The SoftMax reward ablation is removed, while existing SFT, reward-temperature, bonus, memory, and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version documents repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for the reported performance. The new GRPO group-size analysis concerns training samples per prompt, not independent experimental repetitions or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing main benchmark and HM3D-OVON scores are unchanged. New results include NavNuances vertical-movement scores of 22.94 for CompassNav versus 7.88 for its base model, ProcTHOR performance of 58.1 SR/32.8 SPL, and KL/group-size results. The SoftMax result of 31.3 SR/13.1 SPL is deleted.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and Algorithm 1 retain the same mathematical content, including the reward definition, objectives, and action filtering. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central claims: decision understanding through Compass-Data-22k and a gap-aware hybrid reward, strong 7B navigation performance, and real-world transfer. The rewritten introduction and additional experiments elaborate and support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets NavNuances and ProcTHOR results as evidence of structural reasoning and transferable spatial logic. It newly attributes direction/counting weaknesses to task alignment and model scale, and explains fixed-KL stability and the group-size tradeoff. V1's discussion of approximating online-RL feedback through offline training is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds adaptive-KL settings and an explicit reproducibility statement covering the dataset, LoRA weights, and code for generation, training, and deployment. Existing implementation and hardware details remain. The PDFs establish this expanded disclosure, not whether the stated resources are actually accessible.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially recast modular-versus-end-to-end positioning around map fragility, error propagation, and semantic understanding. The dedicated relationship-to-DRL discussion in v1 Appendix A.2 is removed. References also change substantively, including additions for NavNuances, ProcTHOR, Doraemon, and NaviMaster.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and dataset-generation explanation are substantially rewritten. Appendix A is reorganized, and ethics, reproducibility, LLM-use, and acknowledgment statements are added. Author information, headings, and reference presentation also change.

P2.justification: V2 adds three result tables, removes the SoftMax comparison row, and moves the conceptual paradigm figure from v1 Appendix A to the main text as Figure 2. The ICLR template changes the title block, headings, captions, and layout throughout, while existing plots and qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: NavNuances directly tests capabilities that v1 inferred mainly from navigation outcomes, while ProcTHOR and KL/group-size experiments strengthen transfer and sensitivity evidence. However, removing the SoftMax baseline weakens the reward comparison, and the additions provide limited protocol detail and no statistical uncertainty. The broader evidence and clearer release statement provide a qualified, modest net improvement.
